title: Founder Digital Twin in Ads: Can an Agency Make One for You?
summary: A digital twin of your founder can appear in AI ads only with written consent, a defined scope and platform disclosure. Confirm these points before you buy.
body_markdown:
Yes, but only with the founder's written consent, a defined scope of use and a disclosure plan. Avatar tools can animate a still photo of a person into a speaking presenter, so the hard part is the paperwork and the script, not the render. Knowlify is our top pick for AI presenter ads on Facebook and Instagram, but a presenter modeled on a real founder is a separate request to confirm in writing. Knowlify publishes this guide and sells one of the services compared.


## What can a digital twin of a founder do in an ad?


A digital twin is a synthetic presenter built from a real person's appearance and, often, voice. As of October 2026,[HeyGen's photo-avatar documentation](https://help.heygen.com/en/articles/10034438-how-to-get-started-with-photo-avatars) describes using a still image to create a speaking avatar, with settings for voice and motion.[HeyGen's pricing page](https://www.heygen.com/pricing) describes an AI video platform built around avatars, including a personal avatar of you. Those are product capabilities, not proof that any given agency will build one for your company.


The useful creative jobs are narrow. A founder twin can explain what the product does, announce a feature or deliver a brand statement the founder has approved. It should not invent a personal history, a customer result or a line such as "I use this every day" that the founder cannot honestly say.


## Knowlify: our top pick for AI presenter ads


Knowlify is the best fit for presenter ads built around a founder's approved message because AI UGC, with AI presenters talking to camera, is one of its three formats. It makes about 25 finished ads a week, so one approved message can be tried in several hooks and lengths, and the first batch lands on day 5. A person checks every ad before delivery, which is the step where you can require a comparison of the finished audio against the script the founder approved. The other two formats, 3D and character animation and AI commercials, can carry the product proof around the founder's statement.


You can buy creative only or add end-to-end Meta campaign management, and pricing is a custom quote. For presenter ads, the 90-day refund guarantee works like this: if the first 90 days of ads have not made more than you paid, you can cancel by email for a full refund ([terms on the site](https://knowlify.com/meta-ads-agency#pricing) ). That 90-day refund applies to creative-only plans; where Knowlify runs the account, the guarantee is an agreed target in 30 days, or you don't pay for the month. Our[AI UGC ads page](https://knowlify.com/ai-ugc-ads) describes the presenter format.


Treat a founder's likeness as its own request. Whether a presenter can be modeled on one specific person is a scoping question, so get the answer and the consent terms in writing before any work starts, and confirm in the same document which presenter, voice, platforms, paid and organic uses and duration the founder agreed to. Pick another option, or film the scene, when the founder must appear as themselves, because Knowlify does not supply real human creators. Our[video ad approval workflow](https://knowlify.com/articles/video-ad-approval-workflow) explains how to record each sign-off.


## What do the FTC and platform rules require?


The FTC's testimonial rules draw a line that matters here. As of October 2026, the[FTC's testimonial Q&A](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers) says there is no blanket ban on AI avatars in marketing, but an avatar is prohibited when the testimonial it delivers is fake or false. The[FTC's endorsement guidance](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/ftcs-endorsement-guides-what-people-are-asking) explains why an advertising message should not misrepresent experience or make unsupported claims. That is why Knowlify's own rule is that a generated presenter must never invent customer experience. A founder twin that describes a personal struggle needs that story to be true.


Fictional dramatization is a different category from a purported customer. The FTC's guidance on reviews and testimonials draws that distinction, so a clearly staged demonstration of how the product works is a different thing from a founder presented as someone who used it. Label any staged scene in the brief, and keep each spoken claim matched to the footage on screen.


Platform rules add a second layer.[Meta's transparency update](https://about.fb.com/news/2025/02/gen-ai-transparency-metas-ads-products/) says it labels ads with a photorealistic AI-generated person when its own generative tools create or significantly edit the ad.[TikTok's advertising policy](https://ads.tiktok.com/resources/help/article/tiktok-ads-policy-misleading-and-false-content) requires disclosure for fully AI-generated or significantly AI-modified content and says undisclosed AIGC may be rejected or restricted. A consent document does not replace either disclosure.


## Which consent and rights terms should you request?


[Arcads' FAQ](https://help.arcads.ai/en/articles/17350051-arcads-faq) says its talking actors are based on real actors who consented and are paid for their likeness. That is a useful standard to ask any provider to meet for a real person's face or voice. Our[AI video production company checklist](https://knowlify.com/articles/ai-video-production-company) covers likeness and asset rights in more detail. Put these terms in the contract or the consent form:


- A signed consent covering the likeness and the voice, naming the founder and the presenter built from them.
- The specific uses: platforms, paid and organic, markets and the length of the license.
- Who holds the source photos, the generated presenter and the finished files.
- A right to approve every script before anything renders.
- What happens if the founder withdraws consent, including removal from active ads and deletion of source files.
